exposure: migration status (self-defined refugee status, immigrant, non-immigrant)
cohort: The study included 3420 women giving birth in three tertiary care centers in Berlin, comprising 247 with self-defined refugee status, 1356 immigrant women, and 1817 non-immigrant women.
finding: Immigrant women had a higher c-section rate, while women with self-defined refugee status experienced a higher risk for anemia and were less frequently offered epidural anesthesia, with maternal education often explaining more than migration status in multivariate analysis.
mod_finding: Immigrant women showed a higher c-section rate, and women with self-defined refugee status were less often offered epidural anesthesia for pain control during vaginal delivery.
